source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: What is the priority nursing diagnosis for a child with autism?
questions.rationale: Risk for injury is the priority because of self-injury and lack of fear of danger.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Autism (PDF p. 257)
questions.quote: Risk for Injury

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: How should the nurse communicate with a child with autism?
questions.rationale: Use short sentences and provide consistent routines.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Autism (PDF p. 257)
questions.quote: Use of short sentences when talking to the child

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: When should the last daily dose of dextroamphetamine be given?
questions.rationale: Give the last dose early afternoon to prevent insomnia.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, ADHD Drugs (PDF p. 258)
questions.quote: Give last dose early afternoon

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which approach helps a child with ADHD complete schoolwork?
questions.rationale: Provide a quiet space, break tasks into small steps, and keep routines.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, ADHD Interventions (PDF p. 258)
questions.quote: Provide a quiet place free of distractions for ask completion.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which food form suits a hyperactive child who won't sit for meals?
questions.rationale: Finger foods let the child eat while moving.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, ADHD Interventions (PDF p. 259)
questions.quote: Provide finger foods

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A child with mild intellectual disability (IQ 55–69) is described as:
questions.rationale: Mild: educable (reading, writing); moderate: trainable; severe: close supervision; profound: custodial.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Intellectual Disability (PDF p. 259)
questions.quote: Mild 55 – 69 Educable

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which teaching strategy suits a client with intellectual disability?
questions.rationale: Repetition, role modeling, and restructuring the environment help.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Intellectual Disability (PDF p. 259)
questions.quote: Repetition

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client focuses only on the immediate task and needs help to solve problems. Which anxiety level?
questions.rationale: Moderate anxiety narrows the perceptual field; the person can solve problems with assistance.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Anxiety Levels (PDF p. 260)
questions.quote: The person can learn new behavior or solve problems only with assistance

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client in panic may bolt and run. What is the nursing priority?
questions.rationale: Panic causes loss of rational thought and injury risk; safety comes first, with calm presence and reduced stimuli.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Anxiety Levels (PDF p. 260)
questions.quote: The person may bolt and run aimlessly, often exposing himself or herself to injury

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Avoiding places where escape may be difficult is called:
questions.rationale: Agoraphobia is anxiety about places where escape or help may be difficult.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Anxiety Disorders (PDF p. 260)
questions.quote: Anxiety about or avoidance of places or situation from which escape might be difficult

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Generalized anxiety disorder requires excessive worry for a minimum of:
questions.rationale: GAD: persistent excessive worry for at least 6 months.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, GAD (PDF p. 261)
questions.quote: It is characterized by at least 6 month of persistent and excessive worry

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Symptoms after trauma lasting 2 days to 4 weeks suggest:
questions.rationale: Acute stress disorder occurs within 1 month and lasts 2 days to 4 weeks; PTSD persists longer.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Acute Stress Disorder (PDF p. 261)
questions.quote: it last 2 days to 4 weeks

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client thinks, 'This is only anxiety; it will pass,' instead of 'I'm dying.' Which technique?
questions.rationale: Positive reframing turns negative messages into positive ones.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cognitive Techniques (PDF p. 262)
questions.quote: Turning negative message into positive messages

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client snaps a rubber band on the wrist to interrupt negative thoughts. This is:
questions.rationale: Thought-stopping uses techniques like snapping a rubber band to break negative thought cycles.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cognitive Techniques (PDF p. 262)
questions.quote: Snapping a rubber band worn on the wrist

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: 'I feel angry when you turn your back while I'm talking' is an example of:
questions.rationale: Assertiveness training uses 'I' statements to express feelings and needs.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Assertiveness Training (PDF p. 262)
questions.quote: They involve using “I” statement to identify feelings

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which treatment gradually exposes a client to a feared object?
questions.rationale: Systematic desensitization progressively exposes the client in a safe setting until anxiety decreases.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Specific Phobia (PDF p. 263)
questions.quote: The therapist progressive exposes the client to threatening object in a safe setting

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which personality disorder is in Cluster A (odd, eccentric)?
questions.rationale: Cluster A: paranoid, schizoid, schizotypal; B: antisocial, borderline, histrionic, narcissistic; C: avoidant, dependent, OCPD.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Personality Disorders (PDF p. 263)
questions.quote: Includes paranoid, schizoid, and schizotypal personality

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: How should the nurse approach a client with paranoid personality disorder?
questions.rationale: Use a formal, straightforward approach without chit-chat or jokes; involve the client in planning.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Paranoid PD (PDF p. 263)
questions.quote: Approach these clients in a formal, business –like manner

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which defense mechanism is typical of paranoid personality disorder?
questions.rationale: Projection, blaming others for one's difficulties, is characteristic.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Paranoid PD (PDF p. 263)
questions.quote: Uses the defense mechanism of projection

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A detached, emotionally cold client prefers things to people. Which disorder?
questions.rationale: Schizoid PD shows detachment, restricted affect, and few pleasures.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Schizoid PD (PDF p. 263)
questions.quote: Involve themselves more with things than people
